title: J505 corn (AH J505): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: J505 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: J505 corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety for Luzon and Mindanao. About 102 days to harvest, 9.4 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: J505 corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as AH J505 or Asian Hybrid J505. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2018 as NSIC 2018 GMCn 57. Asian Hybrid Seed Technologies bred it. It takes about 102 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 9.36 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

J505 corn takes about 102 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is 3.4 days faster than the average of the 89 yellow GM hybrid corn varieties with a day count, 105.4 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 9.36 t/ha beats the average of its group, 8.13. It sits in the top quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 102 in NSIC trials (GM), 101 to 103 for the conventional version.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its ears grew about 19.67 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 78.15 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears. Against lodging it rated resistant, so it stood up well when wind and rain pushed the plants.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 7.21 t/ha in a DA 10 Bukidnon derby, 5.52 t/ha in DA 12's Sarangani lowland dry season trial, NSIC trials averaged 10.05 t/ha Luzon and 8.67 Mindanao (GM), conventional 7.74 to 8.05.
**Traits in the seed:** YieldGard plus Roundup Ready (events MON810 x NK603): corn borer protection plus glyphosate tolerance, sold as 90:10 bag in bag refuge.
**Season:** Year round if water is adequate.
**Where:** Luzon and Mindanao.
Tall plant with a long ear (about 19 to 20 cm).
Shelling about 78 percent in NSIC trials.
Registry rates the GM version resistant to lodging, corn borer, rust, stalk rot and earworm.
The conventional version was rated highly susceptible to stalk rot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: named by the City of Ilagan corn center among hybrids popular with its farmers, Asian Hybrid's best entry (7.21 t/ha) in a DA 10 derby round. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant J505 corn

It is recommended for Luzon and Mindanao. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is AH J505 the same as J505?
items.a: Yes. AH J505 is another name for J505, registered as NSIC 2018 GMCn 57. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 102 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 9.36 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
It is recommended for Luzon and Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of J505?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
